newsitem.title: USA: US House conferees won't budge on deminimis repeal.
newsitem.headline: US House conferees won't budge on deminimis repeal.

text.p: U.S. House tax conferees, in a first stab at working out differences with the Senate on tax legislation, refused Tuesday to back down from its plan to scale back the two-percent de minimis rule, a House document shows.

House negotiators also refused to adopt a Senate proposal to increase from $10 million to $20 million the arbitrage rebate exception for small issuers of bonds for public school infrastructure projects, according to the House document.
House and Senate conferees are trying to work out differences in their separate bills so that Congress can vote on a single final tax cut measure.

In other provisions, House conferees tentatively refused to adopt the Senate's proposal to repeal altogether the current $150 million cap on non-hospital borrowing by 501(c)(3) groups, according to the House outline.
Instead, the House prefers a tighter plan to raise the limit by $10 million a year for five years - for a total cap of $200 million.
House conferees offered to recede to the Senate on a provision to loosen mortgage revenue bond requirements in disaster areas, the House plan says.

The House's bill would relax standards in disaster areas for 1997 through 1999. The Senate bill loosens the standards in Presidentially declared disaster areas for two years. House conferees said they would go with the Senate plan as long as it gives people two years to place mortgages.
House conferees refused to change tax incentives provisions for the District of Columbia, the document shows.
House and Senate bills include four identical proposals to simplify the tax code for muni issuers. House conferees on Tuesday proposed no changes to that plan.
